title: Finite Group Character Theory Basics
body_html:
Finite Group Character Theory Basics

Standard facts from the ordinary (complex) representation theory of finite groups, collected here as a reusable dependency for the finite Heisenberg–Weil nodes. Let \(H\) be a finite group and let representations be finite-dimensional over \(\mathbb C\). For a representation \(\eta\) of \(H\) write \(\chi_\eta(h)=\operatorname{tr}\eta(h)\) for its character and \(\deg(\eta)=\chi_\eta(1)\) for its degree.

  1. Conjugation invariance. \(\operatorname{tr}\big(\eta(g)\eta(h)\eta(g)^{-1}\big)=\chi_\eta(h)\) for all \(g,h\in H\); in particular \(\chi_\eta\) is a class function.

  2. Central scalars. If \(Z\) is the center of \(H\) and \(\eta|_Z=\xi\) is a character of \(Z\) (i.e. \(\eta(z)=\xi(z)\,\mathrm{id}\) for \(z\in Z\)), then \(\chi_\eta(z)=\xi(z)\deg(\eta)\) and \(|\chi_\eta(z)|=\deg(\eta)\) for all \(z\in Z\).

  3. Irreducibility. The number \(\langle\chi_\eta,\chi_\eta\rangle=\tfrac{1}{|H|}\sum_{h\in H}|\chi_\eta(h)|^2\) is a nonnegative integer, and \(\eta\) is irreducible if and only if \(\langle\chi_\eta,\chi_\eta\rangle=1\).

  4. Character determines representation. Two finite-dimensional representations of \(H\) are isomorphic if and only if they have the same character.

  5. Induction. For a subgroup \(A\le H\) and a representation \(\sigma\) of \(A\), the induced representation \(\operatorname{Ind}_A^H\sigma\) has degree \([H:A]\cdot\deg(\sigma)\); and if \(Z\le A\) with \(Z\) central in \(H\) and \(\sigma(z)=\xi(z)\,\mathrm{id}\) for \(z\in Z\), then \((\operatorname{Ind}_A^H\sigma)(z)=\xi(z)\,\mathrm{id}\) for \(z\in Z\), i.e. \(\operatorname{Ind}_A^H\sigma\) also restricts to \(\xi\) on \(Z\).
